body:
Part of same-project Rust `extract` (D-185, D-187). Separate from moving impl blocks and methods: it is independent, small, and unblocks the CLI and model splits before the larger method-move work.

**Do.**
- When `extract` creates a test container in a target, write `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "<module>_tests.rs"] mod tests;` and put the tests in that sibling file. For a nested target, put the file beside the module's file, e.g. `board/reviews_tests.rs`.
- Tests moved from a `#[path]` container stay in a file.
- If the target already has a `#[path]` container, append the moved tests to it. Today any container already in the target is refused with `E1004`, which blocks a second move into the same module.
- Keep symbol identity. A cargo check failure restores every row, file and history entry, as other moves do.
- No new option: always write a file, since AGENTS.md requires tests in separate files.

**Tests.** A new container writes the header and sibling file; a nested target writes beside the nested module; a second move appends; a `#[path]` source container stays a file; a cargo failure rolls back rows and files; `check --warnings` stays clean.

**Out of scope.** Moving impl blocks or methods apart from their type (T1); Rust `merge` (T2); cross-project `extract`; converting an existing inline container in the target (it keeps today's `E1004`).
title: extract: Rust test containers as files
